summary: LLM API costs can spiral quickly at scale — a customer support bot handling 1M conversations monthly can cost $3,250+/month with flagship models alone. By combining techniques like prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, and output constraints, teams have achieved 50–80% cost reductions in production. Research from PwC in 2026 found prompt caching alone cuts API costs 41–80% across OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, making inference optimization one of the highest-ROI engineering investments for AI-powered products.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (Provider-Native)
techniques.description: Stores computed key-value tensors for repeated prompt prefixes server-side, so cached tokens are billed at a steep discount (up to 90% off input token costs) with no change to model output. Every major provider now offers this natively. Works best when system prompts or large context blocks are stable across requests.
techniques.savings: 41–90% reduction on input token costs for repeated prefixes
techniques.example: Place your 20,000-token RAG knowledge base or detailed system prompt at the top of every request in a fixed order so the static prefix stays identical across calls — Anthropic will cache it after the first request and charge only 10% of normal input cost on subsequent hits.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Intercepts incoming LLM requests, converts them to embeddings, and checks a vector store for semantically similar past queries. If a match exceeds a similarity threshold, the cached response is returned immediately — bypassing the LLM entirely. Most effective for high-repetition query workloads like FAQs and customer support.
techniques.savings: 40–60% reduction in total API calls in high-repetition scenarios; up to 45% cache hit rate reported in production
techniques.example: Deploy GPTCache or Redis Semantic Cache in front of your customer support chatbot — when a user asks 'How do I reset my password?' and a near-identical query was answered 10 minutes ago, the cached answer is returned in milliseconds with zero token cost.

techniques.name: Model Routing
techniques.description: Classifies incoming requests by complexity and routes them to the cheapest model capable of handling them well. Simple tasks like classification, extraction, or short Q&A go to budget models; only complex reasoning or nuanced generation reaches frontier models. Can be rules-based or ML-driven.
techniques.savings: 50–75% reduction in average cost per request depending on workload mix
techniques.example: Using LiteLLM or a custom router, send classification and extraction tasks to GPT-3.5 or Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5 per million tokens), standard queries to GPT-4o-mini or Sonnet 4.6 ($3/$15), and only route complex multi-step reasoning to GPT-4 or Opus — one team achieved a 70/25/5 split that cut costs by over 60%.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces the number of input tokens by removing redundant instructions, trimming few-shot examples, shortening system prompts, and replacing verbose format instructions with compact structured schemas. Every token removed directly reduces cost with no infrastructure change required.
techniques.example: Audit your system prompt and cut it from 800 tokens to under 200 by replacing wordy formatting instructions like 'Please respond in a well-structured, professional manner with clear paragraphs' with a single JSON schema — a 30% prompt length reduction translates directly to 30% lower input costs.

techniques.name: Output Constraints
techniques.description: Limits the number of output tokens generated by setting max_tokens aggressively, enforcing structured output formats (JSON/XML), and instructing the model to be concise. Output tokens are billed at 4–5x the rate of input tokens on flagship models, making output reduction disproportionately impactful.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 in your API call for a summarization task and add 'Respond in 3 bullet points maximum' to your prompt — this eliminated runaway responses and cut output costs by 50% in one documented production case.

techniques.name: Batch API Processing
techniques.description: Groups multiple non-time-sensitive requests into a single batch job processed asynchronously, typically within 24 hours. Providers offer significant discounts for batch workloads since it allows them to optimize GPU utilization. Ideal for offline tasks like data labeling, content generation pipelines, and bulk analysis.
techniques.savings: 50% reduction on API costs for eligible batch workloads
techniques.example: Instead of processing 10,000 product description generations in real-time at standard pricing, submit them via Anthropic's Batch API overnight — you get 50% off, and combined with prompt caching you can achieve up to 95% total cost reduction on those jobs.

techniques.name: Quantized and Smaller Open-Source Models (Self-Hosting)
techniques.description: Running quantized open-weight models locally or on rented GPU infrastructure eliminates per-token API costs entirely. Modern quantized models like Gemma 4 26B A4B or Qwen variants run efficiently on consumer hardware and serve as cost-effective alternatives for tasks where frontier model quality is unnecessary.
techniques.savings: 70–95% reduction vs. frontier API pricing for suitable workloads
techniques.example: Serve a quantized Gemma 4 26B A4B via vLLM on a single 48GB GPU for internal document summarization tasks — you pay only for compute (fixed infrastructure cost) instead of per-token API fees, which breaks even at moderate volume and saves 80%+ at scale.

techniques.name: RAG Optimization and Reranking
techniques.description: Reduces the number of context chunks injected into LLM prompts by using a fast reranker model to select only the most relevant retrieved documents before passing them to the LLM. Cuts input tokens per RAG query substantially while often improving answer quality by reducing noise.
techniques.savings: 20–40% reduction in RAG pipeline input token costs
works_with: Any provider used in RAG pipelines
techniques.example: Instead of passing the top-10 retrieved chunks (potentially 5,000+ tokens) to GPT-4, add a lightweight cross-encoder reranker (e.g., Cohere Rerank or a local model) to select the top-3 most relevant chunks — reducing context from 5,000 to 1,500 tokens per query.

techniques.name: Streaming with Early Termination
techniques.description: Uses streaming responses to detect when sufficient output has been generated and terminates the request early, avoiding paying for tokens the application doesn't need. Particularly useful for classification or intent detection tasks where the answer is clear from the first few tokens.
techniques.savings: 10–40% reduction in output token costs for suitable tasks
techniques.example: For a sentiment classification task, stream the response and close the connection as soon as 'positive', 'negative', or 'neutral' appears in the output — stopping generation at token 5 instead of receiving a 200-token explanation.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified LLM proxy and SDK that provides a single OpenAI-compatible interface to 100+ providers, with built-in model routing, cost tracking, rate limiting, fallbacks, and spend budgets. Enables easy model switching and routing logic without changing application code.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$1,500/month for managed hosting and advanced features

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLM applications. Intercepts LLM API calls, vectorizes queries, and returns cached responses for semantically similar inputs. Supports multiple embedding models and vector stores (FAISS, Redis, Milvus).
tools.pricing_paid: Fully open-source, self-hosted — no paid tier

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Redis-native semantic caching for LLM responses using Redis's vector search capabilities. Stores prompt-response pairs with embeddings and retrieves cached answers for similar queries with configurable similarity thresholds. Part of the Redis AI ecosystem.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis open-source is free; Redis Cloud from $0 (free tier) to pay-as-you-go; Redis Enterprise pricing on request

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and optimization platform that sits as a proxy between your application and LLM providers. Provides cost tracking per request, prompt caching controls, user-level spend analytics, rate limiting, and A/B testing for prompts.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier up to 10,000 requests/month; Pro from $20/month; Team/Enterprise plans available

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Popular LLM application framework with built-in support for caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, semantic), prompt templating, model switching, and chain optimization. Provides a CacheBackedEmbeddings class and LLMCache interface to reduce redundant API calls.

tools.name: Bifrost
tools.description: LLM gateway that combines semantic caching with provider-native prompt caching support, offering a unified layer for cost optimization across OpenAI, Anthropic, and other providers. Designed for production teams needing scalability and reliability alongside caching.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; paid plans on request

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway and observability platform with built-in semantic caching, model fallbacks, automated model routing, prompt management, and detailed cost/latency dashboards. Supports 250+ LLMs through a single API.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10,000 requests/month); Growth from $49/month; Enterprise on request

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source LLM inference engine for self-hosting models. Uses PagedAttention for efficient GPU memory management, continuous batching, and quantization support (AWQ, GPTQ, INT4). Ideal for serving open-weight models behind an API endpoint at scale.
tools.pricing_paid: Fully open-source, self-hosted — infrastructure costs only

tools.name: Cohere Rerank
tools.description: API-based reranking model that scores and reorders retrieved documents by relevance before they are injected into an LLM prompt. Reduces the number of context chunks needed, cutting RAG input token costs while improving answer accuracy.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-use: $1 per 1,000 queries (Rerank 3); free trial credits available

tools.name: Maxim AI
tools.description: LLM evaluation and cost optimization platform that provides prompt testing, token usage analytics, caching strategy recommendations, and production monitoring. Helps teams identify which prompts are over-spending and simulate optimization impact before deployment.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; paid plans from $99/month

quick_wins: Enable provider-native prompt caching immediately by ensuring your system prompt and any static context appear at the top of every request in a fixed, identical order — this requires zero infrastructure change and can cut input costs 41–90% on cached prefixes with Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google.

Set max_tokens explicitly on every API call and add a conciseness instruction to your system prompt (e.g., 'Be brief. Respond in 3 sentences or fewer unless asked to elaborate.') — output tokens cost 4–5x more than input tokens on flagship models, so even a 30% reduction in output length has outsized savings.

Audit and compress your system prompt to under 200 tokens by replacing verbose formatting instructions with a compact JSON schema or single clear example — every 100 tokens removed from a prompt that runs 1M times/month saves $0.25–$7.50 depending on your model tier.

Implement model routing for your lowest-complexity tasks (classification, extraction, yes/no decisions) by switching those calls from GPT-4 or Sonnet to GPT-3.5, Haiku 4.5, or GPT-4o-mini — budget models at $0.25–$1 per million input tokens vs. $15–75 for frontier models make this the fastest ROI routing decision.

Add semantic caching via GPTCache, Redis Semantic Cache, or LangChain's built-in cache for any high-repetition query workload (customer support, FAQ bots, search) — a 45% cache hit rate means nearly half your requests cost nothing, and setup takes under a day with existing Redis infrastructure.
